claims.scope: Same SKU-clustered UCP daily-panel replay as UCP-PANDORA-REPLAY-001. claims.statement: In the frozen September 2026 UCP recall-aware panel replay, adaptive search reliably improves held-out total cost at the current catalog-expansion market rate and at ten times that workload. Search-all reliably improves at zero cost, while one-hundredth and one-tenth of the workload are inconclusive.

claims.scope: Forty title-normalized product decks from one frozen Shopify collection, 24 used for calibration and 16 held out, evaluated across three registered declared real-dollar inspection-cost scenarios. Search-all opens every card and pays every declared inspection cost. The post-collection identity revision limits external interpretation but does not alter the registered held-out calculation.

project.abstract: A shopping agent should search again only when the expected saving can repay the cost of another inspection. We turn that intuition into a costly-search decision rule with a retained incumbent offer, seller-specific price evidence, and a product-level held-out evaluation. Shopify Global Catalog seller decks provide competing offers inside an observed product graph, while UCP direct-merchant panels characterize the wider search surface an agent may expand into. Together, they make the value and cost of another search measurable rather than heuristic. Adaptive stopping is compared with costed search-all on held-out product and SKU clusters. On the UCP panel it reliably lowers total cost at every declared real-dollar workload, while a sensitivity analysis finds search-all favorable at zero cost and no reliable separation at two small positive costs. This shows why material search cost makes selective stopping valuable.
project.subtitle: When is one more merchant inspection worth its cost?
project.title: When Should a Shopping Agent Stop Searching?

preprint.scope: Held-out recall-aware costly-search studies compare adaptive stopping with costed search-all on frozen Shopify and UCP panels. Material declared inspection costs favor selective stopping; zero cost favors search-all and two small positive costs do not reliably separate arms.

pandora.decision_rule: SEARCH iff feasible and E[max(b - P, 0)] > cost
pandora.scenario_assumptions: Declared workload assumptions, not execution telemetry.

2026-09-16.reason: A full same-day rerun fully paginated all 486 eligible merchants but returned zero tracked offers for 276 of them. Relative to September 15, 8,126 of 9,758 comparable offers disappeared across 206 of 309 comparable domains, confirming a coordinated protocol-level retrieval change rather than independently attributable merchant delisting.
